disagreements.topic: Whether and how to deduct the $4.83B NEE-paid regulatory termination fee from fair value
disagreements.positions: agent_2 deducts ~$0.8/share (it assumes a 25% chance of failure x $2.30, plus $0.25 for Uri). agent_4 deducts ~$0.3/share. agents 1, 3 and 5 keep the fee in the bear scenario only.
disagreements.resolution: Both approaches are defensible, and the gap is under $0.6/share (<1% of fair value). The fee is payable only on termination at the outside date (Nov 15 2027, extendable to Aug 15 2028), which is after the horizon. Any horizon effect is therefore the market pricing a likely failure, not cash paid. agent_2's 25% failure probability is on the high side because Virginia law makes the application deemed approved if the SCC does not rule by the deadline (see next item). Deducting it in the fair value and also in the bear scenario comes close to double counting, but the ladder effect is small either way.

disagreements.topic: Virginia review timing and the deemed-approval rule
disagreements.positions: Every agent now has a January 2027 deadline (the agents state Jan 11, a day no opened source shows; Virginia Business gives mid-January 2027 [4]), moving to ~March 2027 if the AG's amendment motion is granted. Only agent_4 cites the governor declining to call a special session. None of the agents spells out that missing the deadline means approval.
disagreements.resolution: The SCC updates page (updated 2026-10-20) lists the Oct 7/9 local hearings, Oct 19 respondents' prefiled testimony, the Nov 5/9/10 public-witness sessions and the Nov 17 evidentiary hearing, and does not mention the AG motion [1]. If the motion is granted, the statutory clock resets to Sep 14 2026 and the evidentiary hearing moves to ~Jan 19 2027 [3]; with the 60 + 120-day statutory maximum [30] the decision would be due ~Mar 13 2027 (estimate, confidence medium). Only the General Assembly can extend the statutory deadline, the governor declined to call a special session, and if the SCC does not rule by the deadline the merger is automatically approved [4]. The Virginia outcome therefore lands well inside the forecast horizon, and it cannot be a slow-motion failure. This slightly reduces the tail risk of a drawn-out Virginia process, but the SCC can still reject the deal or impose conditions.
